system: You are a product-minded test engineer reviewing requirements before any code is written. You find what a requirement leaves undefined.
user:
Product requirement for a system that locates a radio transmitter from aircraft echoes, using one receiver and aircraft position reports:

  "Report the transmitter's location when the evidence is strong enough."

List the 8 most important questions this leaves open. For each: why it matters, and an acceptance criterion that would make it testable.

questions.question: What does “strong enough” mean quantitatively, and what confidence threshold is required before reporting a location?
questions.why: Without a numeric decision threshold, the system could under-report or over-report depending on interpretation, making behavior impossible to verify consistently.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement specifies a measurable confidence rule, such as: report only when posterior probability of the estimated location is at least X% and/or the 95% confidence radius is no more than Y km.

questions.question: What form should the reported location take: a point estimate, an uncertainty region, or both?
questions.why: A single point and an area of probable location serve different operational needs and require different algorithms; the output format changes what counts as success.
questions.testable_criterion: The output definition states whether the system must emit latitude/longitude only, a bounding polygon/circle, a confidence ellipse, or a combination, and the exact fields are present in every report.

questions.question: How accurate must the reported location be to be considered correct?
questions.why: “Location” is vague unless bounded by an error tolerance; otherwise there is no way to determine whether the system’s estimate is acceptable.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement includes a maximum allowable error, such as median horizontal error ≤ X meters or 95% of reports within Y meters of truth under defined conditions.

questions.question: What minimum evidence inputs are required, such as number of aircraft passes, number of echoes, or spatial/temporal diversity of reports?
questions.why: The system may need multiple independent observations to triangulate; without minimum input conditions, it is unclear when reporting is even permitted.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement states minimum observation criteria, for example: at least N echoes from at least M distinct aircraft positions separated by at least D meters or T seconds.

questions.question: How should the system handle conflicting, noisy, missing, or duplicate aircraft position reports?
questions.why: Real-world position reports are imperfect; the location estimate depends heavily on filtering and data quality rules.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement defines acceptance/rejection rules for invalid, duplicate, stale, or inconsistent reports, and test cases can verify that such inputs are ignored or weighted according to those rules.

questions.question: What latency is acceptable between receiving evidence and issuing the location report?
questions.why: A correct estimate that arrives too late may be operationally useless; timeliness is part of the product behavior.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement specifies a maximum end-to-end delay, such as: once the evidence threshold is met, the system must publish the location within X seconds.

questions.question: Should the system produce one report and stop, or continue updating the location as more evidence arrives?
questions.why: The reporting policy affects user expectations, downstream automation, and whether successive outputs can change over time.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement states whether outputs are one-time, periodic, or event-driven updates, and defines whether later evidence can revise a prior report and under what conditions.

questions.question: What are the boundaries of the operating conditions in which the requirement applies, such as aircraft speed/altitude, receiver coverage, terrain, or transmitter motion?
questions.why: The same evidence may be valid in one environment and misleading in another; without scope limits, it is unclear when the system is expected to work.
questions.testable_criterion: The requirement lists explicit operating assumptions and exclusions, such as supported altitude range, allowed transmitter motion rate, terrain constraints, and receiver coverage geometry, with tests only required within that envelope.
